steps.title: Principal orchestrator
steps.summary: Classifies every request, plans, delegates bounded work, inspects each diff itself, runs verification, and owns the outcome.
steps.selects: The default Claude Code model for new sessions. Repositories can override it with claude-codex-init <alias>, and a running session with /model.
steps.shared_note: One continuous session runs every orchestrator step, so they necessarily share a model.

steps.title: Luna
steps.summary: The mechanical worker: narrow, repetitive, well-specified edits and boilerplate.
steps.selects: The Codex model behind the luna profile. Its low reasoning effort defines the role and is not configurable.

steps.title: Terra
steps.summary: The implementation worker: contained features, real bug fixes, multi-file changes, one bounded task per run.
steps.selects: The Codex model behind the terra profile. Its medium reasoning effort defines the role and is not configurable.

steps.title: Vesta
steps.summary: The plan reviewer: challenges a plan before any code is written, when the work is complex or high-risk.
steps.selects: The Codex model behind the vesta profile. Reviewing foundations is cheaper than reviewing consequences, so this may be set independently of the final reviewer.

steps.title: Sol
steps.summary: The final reviewer: fresh read-only sessions that review completed work, and difficult diagnosis.
steps.selects: The Codex model behind the sol profile, used for the review that gates completion.

flow.label: An ordinary request, in your own words
Classify the work
flow.note: Trivial, mechanical, standard, complex, or investigation.

flow.label: Investigation: diagnose, change nothing
flow.note: Read-only sandboxes. Sol may give a second opinion when it materially helps.

flow.label: Inspect the real diff, never the worker's summary
Tests, lint, type checks, build
flow.note: Shell commands. No model runs here.

flow.label: Independent review of the finished work
flow.note: Fresh session, read-only, contained. Always for complex work; for standard work when logic or regression risk warrants it; not for trivial changes.

flow.label: Reproduce each finding, fix, add regression tests
flow.note: Only when a review produced findings that survived verification.

flow.label: Done. Nothing committed without an explicit request
